cards.text: Friend, meet Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:1-3). He tells this one himself, so every "me" is Ezekiel. In the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month, the word of the LORD comes to him.

cards.question: God starts Ezekiel off with a writing job. What does He tell Ezekiel to write down?
God tells Ezekiel why this date matters. On this very day, the king of Babylon has laid ___ to Jerusalem.

cards.text: God gives Ezekiel the news from Jerusalem the very day it happens, and I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS without hearing a single thing. Now God tells him to speak a parable to this rebellious house, and this parable starts in the kitchen. MY kind of parable.

cards.question: The first thing God says in the parable is to put a pot on the fire and pour in water.
With the water in, God names the meat that goes into the pot. Which pieces?

cards.text: Take the choicest of the flock, pile the fuel beneath the pot, bring it to a boil and cook the bones. Friend, when I fire up EVERY oven in this bakery at once, it's because something BIG is coming.
Then the Lord GOD speaks again, and it starts with a woe. Woe to the city of bloodshed, and woe to the pot.

cards.question: God says something is wrong with this pot. What is it?

answers.text: It's rusted and the rust won't come off
It's cracked straight down the side
It's far too small to hold the meat

cards.question: When the pot is emptied piece by piece, God says to cast lots for what comes out.

cards.text: This part's heavy, friend. God says the blood the city shed is still within her.

cards.question: Where does God say the city poured out the blood she shed?
The city poured that blood on the ground and covered it with dust.
God says He placed her blood on the bare rock so it would not be covered. Why does He say He did it?

answers.text: To stir up wrath and take vengeance
To warn the nations all around
To call the priests to pray

cards.text: Back to the pot, friend, and that line again: "Woe to the city of bloodshed!" Then the Lord GOD says, "I, too, will pile the kindling high."
Logs piled on, fire kindled, meat cooked well, spices mixed in. I've run some hot ovens in my day, but this fire is turned all the way UP.

cards.question: With the fire roaring like that, what does God say about the bones in the pot?

cards.text: Then the empty pot goes onto the coals until it gets hot and its copper glows.

cards.question: What does God say all that heat will do to the empty pot?

answers.text: Melt its impurity and burn off its rust
Make it shine bright for a feast
Harden it so it never cracks

cards.question: The fire finally gets the thick rust off the pot.

cards.text: God says the pot has frustrated every effort, and friend, I KNOW that pan: midnight, sticky cookie sheet, I soak it, I scrub it, I give it a whole PEP TALK. Then God stops describing the pot and starts saying "you."

cards.question: Because of the indecency of their uncleanness, God says He tried to ___ them, but they would not be purified from their filthiness.
God says they will not be pure again until when?

answers.text: Until His wrath against them subsides
Until the king of Babylon leaves
Until they bring a new offering

cards.text: Then God closes it out: "I, the LORD, have spoken; the time is coming, and I will act."

cards.question: God says He may still relent and hold back.
God says He will judge them according to what?

findings.problem: The blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. 'Laid siege to', 'laid claim to' and 'laid waste to' are all common phrases, and no earlier card says anything about an army or a siege. A baker can only guess which phrase the verse uses.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ('God gives Ezekiel the news…', 'Now God tells him…', 'MY kind of parable.'). It also carries more than two beats: the same-day news with the drawer joke, the order to speak a parable to the rebellious house, and the kitchen setup.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 4 says 'this parable starts in the kitchen' right before card 5 asks whether the parable starts with a pot on the fire. The setup line all but hands the baker 'True'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The two wrong answers ('Only the leftover scraps', 'The pieces nobody wants') mean nearly the same thing. 'Every good piece' is the only answer that differs, so it stands out and the baker can pick it by elimination.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke ('when I fire up EVERY oven in this bakery at once, it's because something BIG is coming') is pleasant but not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: In 24:6, the pot is in apposition to the city: 'Woe to the city of bloodshed, to the pot now rusted'. The pot is the city. 'Woe to the city of bloodshed, and woe to the pot' turns it into two separate woes and hides the one link the text states between the parable and its meaning.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke ('I've run some hot ovens in my day, but this fire is turned all the way UP') reads as mildly pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says 'their uncleanness' and 'cleanse them', but nothing in the question says who 'them' is. Card 7, which isn't on screen anymore, only says God starts saying 'you'. The rewording also turns the text's 'you' into 'them'.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'God says they will not be pure again until when?' The question never says who 'they' are, and the right answer says 'against them'.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'God says He will judge them according to what?' The question never says who 'them' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The size of their city' is silly as a basis for God's judgment. It doesn't match the tone of 'Their ways and deeds' and is easy to rule out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
